description: We are Team Chronos, a group of 10th graders from Bangladesh, driven by curiosity and the desire to make a difference. We are passionate about exploring science, technology & data to understand the world around us and solve real-life problems.
summary: TORONGO is a bilingual (English/Bangla) mobile and web prototype that helps water and land resource managers explore river and surface change using satellite-radar observations, with Bangladesh’s Jamuna River corridor as its demonstration area. Designed around eight feature areas—Sky Calendar, Delta, Duet, Spot Check, Trust Ledger, Evidence Brief, AI Advisor, and Community Page—it brings NASA NISAR observation discovery, Sentinel-1/OPERA comparison context, satellite browse imagery, and rainfall context into one interface. Users can inspect acquisition metadata and product maturity, explore visual layers, review evidence limitations, and prepare a shareable brief. TORONGO aims to make complex radar information easier to navigate while separating observed information from derived results and proposed interpretations. The current prototype does not yet calculate validated flood extent or cross-sensor statistics; it supports post-observation exploration, not flood forecasting or warnings.
details:
TORONGO is designed for water and river-resource managers who need a simpler and more transparent way to explore satellite observations of rivers and surrounding land. Bangladesh’s Jamuna River corridor is the project's demonstration area.

The application follows a NISAR-first observation workflow. Users can select an area and explore available satellite observations. The Sky Calendar workflow uses NASA Common Metadata Repository (CMR) requests to discover NISAR Level-2 GCOV validated and provisional scene metadata, as well as NASA OPERA RTC-S1 Sentinel-1 metadata. This provides information such as acquisition dates, scene identifiers, and product maturity.

The project is organised around eight feature areas:

1. Sky Calendar: Discover available observations and inspect acquisition dates and data maturity.

2. Delta: Explore before-and-after views and river or surface-change concepts.

3. Duet: Explore the differences between NISAR L-band and Sentinel-1 C-band radar observations.

4. Spot Check: Inspect a selected location and its supporting evidence.

5. Trust Ledger: Understand where information comes from using the labels Observed, Derived, and Proposed.

6. Evidence Brief: Prepare a shareable summary containing observation and evidence information.

7. AI Advisor: Explain radar concepts and application information in accessible language.

8. Community Page: Provide a prototype space for discussion and sharing local observations.

The current prototype connects to NASA services for observation metadata, visual browse imagery, and rainfall context. NASA GIBS supplies map imagery for visual exploration, while NASA POWER provides daily point-precipitation context. The application also includes English and Bangla text structures, evidence and provenance screens, and a brief preview/export workflow.

An important distinction is that the current prototype does not yet process NISAR or Sentinel-1 raster pixels into validated flood maps or calculate measured flood area, riverbank movement, flooded-cropland area, cross-sensor IoU/kappa statistics, or ground displacement. These outputs are not presented as established results. The current Advisor is a deterministic, keyword-based explainer using static reference text, and the Community Page is a local prototype rather than a production service with persistent accounts and moderation.

Technology used: JavaScript, React, React Native, Expo SDK 54, NASA CMR, NASA GIBS WMS, NASA POWER Daily API, React Native SVG, Expo Linear Gradient, Expo Print, Expo Sharing, and Google Fonts packages including Inter, Manrope, and Noto Sans Bengali.

TORONGO’s creative approach is to combine satellite-observation discovery with understandable evidence presentation. It makes the source, maturity, and limitations of observations visible instead of treating every image or interpretation as a confirmed measurement. The team considered sensor differences, observation dates, data maturity, missing coverage, the distinction between browse imagery and analytical results, bilingual accessibility, and the need to keep proposed interpretations separate from observed information.

TORONGO is intended as a post-observation exploration and evidence-organisation tool. It is not a flood prediction, early-warning, or emergency-response system.
